_comment: Comparison data for tools/build_compare_more.py. Competitor facts only from their own App Store listings or sites (sources). Checked 7 Nov 2026.

nutrition.name: MyFitnessPal
nutrition.title: MyFitnessPal alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and MyFitnessPal compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a MyFitnessPal alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and MyFitnessPal side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: MyFitnessPal alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and MyFitnessPal compared
nutrition.lead: MyFitnessPal is one of the best known calorie counters, with a very large food database. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition, using each company's own published information.
nutrition.who: Anyone counting calories and macros, with Premium and Premium Plus tiers.
nutrition.price: Free to download. Premium and Premium Plus are in-app purchases. The Australian App Store lists them from $14.99 to $129.99 (monthly and yearly), without saying which price is which tier.
nutrition.free: Free food logging with the full database, macro goals, water and activity tracking. The listing says Premium is ad-free, which suggests the free version has ads.
nutrition.food_database: Over 20.5 million items, including restaurant dishes.
nutrition.ai_logging: Meal scanning and voice logging on Premium.
nutrition.micronutrients: The App Store description doesn't mention vitamins and minerals.
nutrition.coaching: Custom macro goals on Premium. Personalised meal plans, grocery delivery and 1,000+ recipes on Premium Plus.
nutrition.apps: iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch on the App Store, with Wear OS integration.
nutrition.currency: Australian App Store prices shown in $.
them_better: A food database of over 20.5 million items, including restaurant dishes.
Photo and voice logging on Premium.
Personalised meal plans and grocery delivery on Premium Plus.
us_better: You want barcode scanning without paying (7 scans a week on Free, unlimited on Nutrition).
You want Australian Food Composition Database foods first, and a full vitamin and mineral breakdown against Australian recommended intakes.
You want a free version with no ads, and prices in Australian dollars.

nutrition.name: MacroFactor
nutrition.title: MacroFactor alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and MacroFactor compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a MacroFactor alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and MacroFactor side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: MacroFactor alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and MacroFactor compared
nutrition.lead: MacroFactor is a paid macro tracker known for its adaptive coaching, which adjusts your targets from your intake and weight. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition.
nutrition.who: People tracking macros who want targets that adapt to their metabolism.
nutrition.price: US$71.99 a year (about US$5.99 a month) per its App Store description. Monthly and other plans are also offered in the store.
nutrition.free: No free version. Free to download with a 7 day trial.
nutrition.food_database: A large verified food database (size not stated).
nutrition.ai_logging: AI label scanning for custom foods and photo or text recipe import. Voice logging isn't mentioned.
nutrition.coaching: A dynamic algorithm adapts your targets to changes in your metabolism.
nutrition.apps: iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch on the App Store.
them_better: Adaptive targets that adjust from your weight and intake.
A verified food database built for accuracy.
An ad-free app built around macro coaching.
us_better: You want a free version to keep using after the trial.
You want Australian Food Composition Database foods first, and nutrients measured against Australian recommended intakes.
You want a grocery list from your meal plan and prices in Australian dollars.

nutrition.name: Cronometer
nutrition.title: Cronometer alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Cronometer compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a Cronometer alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and Cronometer side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: Cronometer alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Cronometer compared
nutrition.lead: Cronometer is a nutrition tracker known for detailed vitamin and mineral tracking from a curated database. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition.
nutrition.who: People who want detailed nutrient tracking, with a free version and a Gold upgrade.
nutrition.price: Free. Gold US$10.99 a month or US$59.99 a year on the US App Store.
nutrition.free: Free version with barcode scanning. Gold removes ads and adds photo and voice logging, a fasting tracker, a recipe importer and more.
nutrition.food_database: More than 1.1 million verified foods in a curated database.
nutrition.ai_logging: Photo and voice logging, where AI identifies foods and estimates portions, on Gold.
nutrition.coaching: Crono Coach and deeper insights on Gold.
nutrition.apps: iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch on the App Store.
nutrition.currency: US dollars on the US App Store.
them_better: Photo and voice logging on Gold.
us_better: You want Australian Food Composition Database foods first, with nutrients measured against Australian recommended intakes.
You want a weekly meal plan that writes your grocery list, grouped by supermarket aisle.
You want a free version with no ads, and prices in Australian dollars.

nutrition.name: Easy Diet Diary
nutrition.title: Easy Diet Diary alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Easy Diet Diary compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a Easy Diet Diary alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and Easy Diet Diary side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: Easy Diet Diary alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Easy Diet Diary compared
nutrition.lead: Easy Diet Diary is an Australian food diary from Xyris, with an Australian food database. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition.
nutrition.who: Australians who want a simple, free food diary.
nutrition.price: Free. The App Store listing says it is completely free with no ads.
nutrition.free: The whole app is free, with no ads.
nutrition.food_database: An extensive Australian food database based on official sources.
nutrition.ai_logging: No AI logging mentioned. You can attach photos to diary entries.
nutrition.micronutrients: Energy, protein, fat and carbs, plus sodium, potassium, calcium and phosphorus.
nutrition.apps: iPhone and iPad on the App Store.
them_better: It's completely free, with no ads.
An Australian food database from an Australian developer.
us_better: You want a full vitamin and mineral breakdown measured against Australian recommended intakes.
You want a weekly meal plan that writes your grocery list, plus weight, progress photos and streaks.
You want to describe a meal in plain words and have Tali log it for you to check.

nutrition.name: Lose It!
nutrition.title: Lose It! alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Lose It! compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a Lose It! alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and Lose It! side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: Lose It! alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Lose It! compared
nutrition.lead: Lose It! is a calorie counter built around weight loss, with a large food database. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition.
nutrition.who: People who want to lose weight with a calorie budget.
nutrition.price: Free basic version. Premium is an in-app purchase; the US App Store lists prices from US$9.99 to US$79.99, and lifetime from US$49.99, without saying which is monthly or yearly.
nutrition.free: Free calorie tracking, a weight loss plan and community support.
nutrition.ai_logging: Photo meal logging and AI voice logging on Premium.
nutrition.micronutrients: Vitamins and minerals in Premium's advanced tracking.
nutrition.coaching: A weight loss plan on Free. Meal planning and targets, and diet plans on Premium.
nutrition.apps: iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch on the App Store.
nutrition.currency: US dollars on the US App Store.
them_better: A database of 56+ million items and recipes.
Photo and AI voice logging on Premium.
us_better: You want barcode scanning on the free version (7 scans a week, unlimited on Nutrition).
You want vitamins and minerals measured against Australian recommended intakes without a premium tier for advanced tracking.
You want Australian Food Composition Database foods first, and prices in Australian dollars.

nutrition.name: Carb Manager
nutrition.title: Carb Manager alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Carb Manager compared
nutrition.desc: Looking for a Carb Manager alternative in Australia? Totality Nutrition and Carb Manager side by side: price, free version, food database, barcode scanning, AI logging and nutrients.
nutrition.h1: Carb Manager alternative in Australia: Totality Nutrition and Carb Manager compared
nutrition.lead: Carb Manager is a keto and low carb tracker with free net carb tracking. Here is how it lines up with Totality Nutrition.
nutrition.who: People on keto or low carb diets who track net carbs.
nutrition.price: Free to use. Premium is an in-app purchase; the US App Store lists options from US$8.49 a month to US$49.99, without saying which are current.
nutrition.free: Free net carb, calorie and macro tracking, unlimited barcode scans, water, exercise and weight.
nutrition.micronutrients: Micronutrients on Premium, with goals for 30+ nutrients.
nutrition.coaching: Keto recipes, carb cycling, a fasting app and advanced reports on Premium.
nutrition.apps: iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch on the App Store.
nutrition.currency: US dollars on the US App Store.
them_better: Built around keto and net carbs.
us_better: You want vitamins and minerals measured against Australian recommended intakes on your plan, not a premium add-on.
You want Australian Food Composition Database foods first.
You want a weekly meal plan with a grocery list grouped by supermarket aisle, and prices in Australian dollars.
